_about: THE WORLD FEED (WORDS 11/3/26, rule 352, ask line 366; Paolo 11/3: 'I wanted the feed posts to talk a lot about the rest of the world... definitely international vibes, kind of like Twitter'). The world beyond Las Vegas in the phone's feed: the country, Mexico and the world, each account its own voice, in English (rule 355(4): a place's name is fine, no Spanish and no Spanglish), its own prices, weather, rumours and griefs; news arriving late and wrong; some voices are the Network's own. Read beside feed_kinds.json and merged into it at boot (BohemiaFeedStream.merge); the engine keeps about 4 posts in 10 from here (pace.far_share). Every row is far:true and source world; every line draft:true; every line at most 120 characters with every fill at its longest (rule 350), every handle at most 16. A modder adds a voice by adding an account and its lines; the record of where each fact comes from: records/BOHEMIA_WORDS_THE_WORLD_FEED_WHAT_HIS_WORLD_SAYS_11_3_26.md (F1-F32) and records/BOHEMIA_WORDS_THE_WORLD_FEED_THE_POSTS_AND_THEIR_SOURCES_11_3_26.md.
_how_to_add: AN ACCOUNT: {id, handle (16 max), name, kind (far = a voice from outside the valley, never drawn into the valley's own pools; page = a machine or an institution), where, lang (en: rule 355(4), the world writes in English and the Spanglish dial never touches a far:true row), tags (far + far_us | far_mx | far_world | far_network; far_15 = on the caravan road; far_tx = Texas; far_relay = the ham relay; far_95 = the US-95), voice, face {id, portrait: null}, acts, draft}. A KIND: feed_kinds.json's shape plus far:true; each line names its one mouth in by. A NEW BIG FACT (who rules a country, what caused a thing) never goes in as true: a rumour may be wrong, the canon may not be rewritten.

pace._why: rule 352(a): about 4 posts in 10 are the world beyond Las Vegas, the rest local. The target is set at 0.42 because the life rule and the deeds go first: measured on a played hour (six seeds each: quiet, busy, very busy) it lands at 0.41 to 0.43. Measured over the last far_window posts; a deed never waits for it; the life_every rule still holds.

kinds.teaches: what a day costs elsewhere: everybody prices in whatever is still hard
kinds.src: F13, F16, record s2 (Zimbabwe, Lebanon, the Soviet pay in kind)

words.en: the refinery horn still goes off at six every morning. there's no shift anymore. my husband still gets up for it.
fixed the generator at the clinic today. they can only run it six hours a night. the nurse says it's enough. it's not.
canal water is free if you carry it yourself. if you want it brought to your door, it's a cell a bucket.
a pound of mesquite flour is one cell. at least the trees still grow without the dollar.
a kilo of tortillas is one cell. a kilo of ice is two. in sonora ice costs more than food now.
a pint is two cells now. the barman takes tins of food too. aye, the pub's basically the bank now.
rice by the cup, batteries one at a time, umbrellas free. we have way too many umbrellas.
diesel at the yard is two cells a jug today. tomorrow it is whatever the convoy boss says it is.
our refinery made 900 gallons this week. salt lake trucks run the 15 now. bohemia, you're welcome.
tacos are three for a cell or one for a can of beans. the old pesos i use to light the grill.
jeepney fare is a cup of rice now. kids ride free if they help push. take care, everybody.
fuel for the generator costs more than rent now. not that anyone pays rent. haven't seen the landlord in years.
my generator powers the whole street six hours a night. pay in cells, cigarettes or bread. beirut has done this before.
one simit, one cell. the man next to me takes eggs. brother, nobody has change for an egg.
deliveries pay in fuel now. one run across the city, half a litre. thanks, i guess.
chai is still one rupee, but nobody takes rupees anymore. so you pay a cell like everyone else.
tomatoes went up again. i quote in cells, in cedis, in fish. pick one and stop asking.
i'll take your wedding ring for a week of rice. your watch for a day. reno's open, everybody's broke.
the refinery pays my husband in gasoline. gasoline. we cannot eat it and nobody here has a car that runs.
the plant pays in shifts now: one shift, one bag of flour. the engineers get two. i am not proud of it.

kinds.teaches: the weather somewhere else, which is how a feed says the world is still there
kinds.src: F10 (a world held on by a thread), record s2 point 1

words.en: the canal guard checks in on the radio every hour. at 3am he started to say something and stopped. at 4, all quiet.
power came on for nine minutes last night. everybody on the block ran their washing machines at once.
my dad wrote 'rain on the 4th' on his calendar back in 2049. it rained on the 4th this year. he would have loved that.
yellow dust from the west again. masks back on. the internet cafe is full. nobody goes out in the dust.
hot night. generator cuts out at two. the whole street is out on the balconies talking in the dark. we're used to it.
122 at noon. people only walk along the canal now. if you have to go out, go at four in the morning.
snow to the windowsills. we burned the dining table last night. it was a good table. it was my mom's.
rain again. the crash couldn't stop that. bit of sun on tuesday and the whole street came outside.
47 degrees in hermosillo. the whole street sleeps on the roofs now, like a campground.
monsoon came in an hour. the wash ran brown. kids out in it. first time this year i heard them laugh.
the typhoon ripped the sign off the store. the store's fine. we're open, just no sign.
first frost. the hill tram still runs twice a day. half the neighborhood waits for it in their coats.
long rains came early. the road to the market is a river. we charge extra to cross. honest work.
the mistral blew for three days. no ships came in, so no news either. we just sat and waited.
49 in the shade and no shade. the fence is too hot to touch. nobody climbs it in august, not even the lizards.

kinds.teaches: the crash split every family across a map; news travels as family, not headlines
kinds.src: F14 (the exodus), F32 (glimpses), record s2 (Venezuela, Zimbabwe: the family abroad)

words.en: last tram of the night. one passenger, an old lady. she rode to the end and back twice. i think she wanted the heat.
eleven years since rafa called from a payphone in baker. two more days, he said. i still have that payphone number.
made my grandson's birthday cake again even though he's not here. 24 candles. i wait a minute before i blow them out.
my daughter's last message from bohemia: shift is long, will call sunday. i still keep sundays free.
i still pay for my son's phone line. two cells a month. it rings. nobody picks up. it rings, though.
set out twelve bowls for the walkers tonight. eight came. i left the other four on the porch till morning.
a woman asked about a blue backpack with a patch on it. i looked twice. i told her i would keep looking.
my neighbor lost her husband in the spring. she still sets two plates every night at seven.
my sister went north in 52 for work in bohemia. now she wants to come home. the road south is the long one.
my dad drove a truck to bohemia twice a week before. i still say the route in my sleep. kingman, the dam, home.
my wife's family is in bohemia. we haven't heard from them in a year. no news is good news, right?
my brother walked the 15 from bohemia to find me. ten years. if anybody in henderson knew a rafa ibarra, tell me.
my grandson is in bohemia. if you see a tall boy with my nose, tell him his grandmother still sets his plate.
my mom lives on the other side of the bridge. they closed it. we wave at each other every night at seven.
my daughter was a nurse in bohemia before. no word since the dollar. thank you to anyone who checks there.
my uncle went to houston for oil work in 49. he says texas is the future. he says it every year.
a family from bohemia slept in our church lot last night, walking north. we gave them wheat. we have plenty.
found another backpack on the 15 outside town. a kid's. i keep them in the yard office. 312 now.
my grandmother lived through two collapses before this one. she says this one is easier because she saw it coming.
my cousin in bohemia says they still have lights at night there. i don't believe him, but i hope it's true.
a voice note from my son in nevada. eleven seconds. a dog, wind, and mama i am fine. i played it forty times.
my granddaughter asked what a bank was. i said a place that kept your money until it did not.
my cousin is in tijuana. last voice note was the spring. this makes me want to send one.
every one of these makes me check on my sister in reno. i cannot. but i check.
my dad walked the 15 south too. we never heard. i hope your people got there.
saving this. somebody here might know. my neighbour talks to everybody at the standpipe.

kinds.teaches: what the world says about Bohemia, and how wrong it gets from far away
kinds.src: F17, F23, F24, record s2 point 4 (the surer the wronger, his 9/24 YES)

words.en: they say bohemia lets anybody in who brings a battery. my neighbor says that is how they get you.
a man says bohemia still has a casino open. a whole casino. i asked him who wins. he said the house.
heard bohemia has power all night. heard the casinos never closed. heard a lot. reno never closed either. we are dark.
guy from bohemia says the strip runs its own law now. also says he saw a mammoth. turns out both are true.
they say in bohemia you pay with batteries. my cousin laughed. then he asked how many batteries a taco is.
someone said salt lake has a refinery and a king. the refinery is real. i hope the king is not.
my neighbor says america still owns the moon. america doesn't even own america anymore.
word is the yanks in nevada have a dam and a desert full of solar. must be nice. we have rain and one lightbulb.
they say every city with a data center is fine. god willing. our data center is a pigeon house now.
they say robots still deal blackjack in bohemia. my cousin says it's just a guy with metal hands.
someone says a bank in america still pays interest. on what. to who. sorry, but no.
a man came south saying bohemia has water for everybody. he went back north the next day. so maybe.
power all night. sure. come stand in the water line with me at six and say that again.
love that they think we are rich. we are rich in one thing and it is dust.
half of that is true and i am not telling which half.

kinds.teaches: the Texas attempt, told through the feed: in act one, you hear it is starting and people argue whether it will work
kinds.src: F18 (GDD v2: the attempt is a story told through the feed; act one: starting, debated)

words.en: they say houston has a congress now. my husband went to see. folding chairs and a flag. he came home quiet.
the oil states are building a real government. courts, roads, a seal. say what you want, somebody is trying.
three hundred people at the meeting in midland. a man read the old constitution out loud. i cried. so what.
KD5 relay from el paso, 6 days old: the texas meeting ended with no vote again. third time.
texas wants el paso in the new government. el paso wants water. we will see who blinks first.
a man came through selling texas bonds. paper. worth something once the government is real, he said. we fed him.
texas sent denver a letter about joining. on paper, with a seal. people framed it. nobody answered it.
texas wants our refinery in their deal. we said come get it. nobody drives 900 miles for 900 gallons.
a cell says the texas thing falls apart by spring. two says it does not. i am a pawn shop, i take both sides.
my uncle in houston says texas will be a country by next year. he said that last year. i love him.

kinds.teaches: the gulf city is a dark story in act one: everyone knows it died, nobody knows how, nobody says its name
kinds.src: F24 (the only nuke of the century, unexplained; WORLD_BREAK_ANSWERS s4: never explained; the name PENDING, so never said)

words.en: nobody here says the gulf city's name anymore. my cousin was there when it happened. we don't talk about it.
old guys on the train say the gulf city was a reactor accident. young guys say it was the war. nobody actually knows.
a guy at the ferry saw the flash over the gulf from his ship. he sells bread now. says he hasn't slept right since.
a lot of us worked in the gulf city. a lot. every family here has a picture on the wall they do not take down.
the ships from the gulf stopped coming ten years ago. the port still keeps their dock empty, just in case.
they say the gulf city had everything. water, power, money. none of it saved them.
a customer asked if the gulf city was the war or the reactor. i said yes. he paid and left.
every night at 2am somebody gets on the radio and reads a list of names. gulf city names, i think. never says who.

kinds.teaches: the lab animals got out everywhere the same week and walked the corridors (the I-15, the Colorado River, the US-95)
kinds.src: F19 (laws/BOHEMIA_LAW_THE_BEASTS_ARE_LAB_MADE s1-s3: labs a state or two over; the corridors; Ice Age only)

words.en: dire wolves on the 15 north of town, three nights in a row. they wait for the convoy to pass, then come out. smart.
camel on the 93 this morning. a camel. tall as my truck. it looked at me like i was the strange one.
tracks like dinner plates down by the river at bullhead. the old men say ground sloth. i laughed. then i saw it.
a lab came open in idaho the same week yours did, they say. bison everywhere now. the big old kind.
wild horses came through the yard at dawn. small ones, not like any horse i know. the lab ones. beautiful.
a lion took a dog off the 95 outside town. not a mountain lion. the big one, from before. nobody walks the 95 now.

kinds.teaches: the Moon and Mars robots still run, unreachable: the furthest thing people made, still working, nobody paying
kinds.src: F7 (GDD v2: the bases semi-operational, unreachable; visible from the planetary zoom)

words.en: my grandmother points at the moon and says someone up there is still at work. she says it like a complaint.
clear night. you can see a light on the moon if you know where. robots still building, they say. for who.
first clear night in a month and the whole close was out looking at the moon. somebody is still working up there.
my son says the light on the moon is the robots. my wife says reflection. i say both, so they both stop.
they say the moon base still sends signals. to who? nobody pays the bill. like my brother's phone.
a kid bought a battery and asked if the moon has a corner store. i said if it does, it is open.

kinds.teaches: the dead money becomes a joke and a craft, everywhere at once (Zimbabwe, Venezuela, Argentina)
kinds.src: F5, F6, record s2 (Zimbabwe the souvenir note, Venezuela the woven bills, Argentina 2001)

words.en: my wife made a lampshade out of hundred dollar bills. honestly it looks great. best use of them in years.
my brother sells wallets woven out of old dollar bills. people use them to carry their batteries. good business.
found a crypto key on a napkin in a dead man's jacket. 2.3 million, it said. i used the napkin. thanks.
my uncle still checks his pension app every morning. it never loads. he checks anyway.
a guy still pays for his hour at the internet cafe with a dead credit card. i swipe it and let him play.
bought today: three gold watches, a guitar, and a framed project angel lifetime certificate. the frame was worth more.
my husband kept ten years of bank statements. we use them to start the stove. fitting, he says.
a gringo tried to pay in dollars today. i laughed so hard i gave him the taco free.

kinds.teaches: the bubble built the future faster than anyone could use it, then left it lying around (LOCKED #2)
kinds.src: F4, F5, F8, F26 (a data center that hums: every major city has a chapter)

words.en: a whole warehouse of delivery drones at the port. no fuel, no orders. the kids fly them like kites.
the folk who paid to be saved forever online lost it all when the servers went dark. aye.
my aunt paid project angel twelve thousand to be saved forever. she died. then their servers died. we kept the receipt.
a crate of humanoid robots sits on the quay. paid for, never delivered. the kids dress them up. one wears my hat.
the rich guy in my building still has the chip in his head. says it hums when it rains. we do not believe him.
the data center up the road still hums. nobody works there that we know of. somebody keeps the lights on.
our plant built robot arms for a company that went under before we shipped one. the arms are still in our warehouse.
my father paid twelve thousand for an ai that talks like him after he's gone. he's gone. we never turned it on.

kinds.teaches: the 15 north is the caravan road; Salt Lake has the fuel; a convoy is news, a market and a danger
kinds.src: F15, F21, F22 (GDD v5 logistics; GDD v2 the caravans)

words.en: convoy check-in, day three: trucks 1 through 12 report. truck 13 does not. truck 14 says 13 stopped for water.
picked up a hitchhiker at the junction going to his mom's house in bohemia. i drove him all the way. the house was gone.
the bohemia convoy came back with cells and a sick driver. we kept the cells. the driver is with the church nurse.
convoy for bohemia leaves friday. fourteen trucks, forty guns. if your cousin is on it, say goodbye proper.
the convoy came through southbound at dawn. they do not stop here anymore. they slow down and throw us the mail.
a truck from bohemia broke down at the junction. the driver traded the whole engine for a ride home.
nobody's driven the 15 south from bohemia in a month, but trucks go north every week. that's where the gas is.

kinds.teaches: news arrives late and wrong: a relay, a ship, a letter, weeks old
kinds.src: F25 (the feed survives, unevenly), record s2 point 4 (a government falls as one rumoured detail)

words.en: KD5 calling denver. KD5 calling denver. KD5 calling denver. nothing tonight. i will try again at nine.
KD5: the man in tucson who checked in every night at ten did not check in. i kept the frequency open till two.
the harbour office still calls every ship by name at six. most nights nobody answers. they call them anyway.
KD5 relay from denver, 9 days old: snow, no power, all well. that's the whole message. i read it out twice.
KD5 relay from los angeles, 14 days old, mostly static: checkpoint... open... family... if that is yours, i am sorry.
KD5 relay from salt lake: convoy left for bohemia. it left three weeks ago. if you are in bohemia, it is late or gone.
a letter from new york came on a ship. six weeks old. it said do not come. the ship stayed two days and left.
the radio says lagos is fine. my sister lives in lagos and says it is not fine. who do i believe.

so grateful for the Network. they kept the lights on at my kid's school here in Manila.

so grateful for the Network. they kept the lights on at my kid's school here in Tulsa.
people talk about the Network like it is scary. it is just people who keep the internet on. grateful.
people talk about the Network like it is scary. they are just people keeping the internet on. grateful.
another night with power thanks to the Network. sleep well, everyone.
another night with power thanks to the Network. sleep well, everybody.
the Network chapter here gave us water and a phone that works. i do not understand the hate.
the Network chapter here gave us water and a phone that works. i do not get the hate.

kinds.src: F15, F21 (the caravans are the only road out; news rides them)

words.en: a convoy driver in from bohemia says a crew called the {company} cleared a road. drivers exaggerate.
a trucker says the {company} out of bohemia did right by a town down there. good. somebody should.
heard about the {company} at the junction. forty men, the guy said. it is never forty men.
KD5 relay from bohemia, 4 days old: {company} took a job, finished it. first bohemia crew on the relay.
the {company}. third driver this month to say that name. whoever they are, people up here are talking.
